title: Media and Arts
description: Two ways of reaching people set side by side - the library, which has lasted for millennia, and the pop single, which lasted about fifty years: the words on the shelves (monographs, dictionary, catalogue, newspapers, journals against magazines, and the French journal that is an English newspaper), the argued plea for libraries by Lois E. Hole and its five steps from librarians as the heroes of civilization to the education she would give, and the means it uses to argue - reasoning and quotation, and not one statistic in the whole text; the vocabulary of that argument (civilization, an era, the lifeblood, to explore, to enlighten, expansion, crafts, literacy, a shortage, to pay tribute to, to wonder); parallel change - the double the, two comparatives tied to each other, in both directions since the book's own last item goes down, with the comparative to choose for short words, long words, countable and uncountable quantities, and the reason the structure must be called parallel change rather than parallel increase; the newspaper analysis of why the single stopped selling, read as a document of 2002 with its figures dated (400,000 singles in a week, the worst in 35 years, a fall of 8.7 per cent, Eminem the only artist past five million) and the words that carry it (a casualty, a passion, to blame, to shun, a decline, to plunge, a performance, to release, to surpass, a track, supremacy); some and any and all their compounds, with the honest account of why the same question appears in the book with both - some making it an offer, any a neutral question - and the two traps of form after a negative verb and after hardly; the blocks of a formal letter of enquiry and the punctuation of To Whom It May Concern; and the AABBA shape of a limerick
